entries.title: At the Hearth, the morning light spills across the common room as Wren turns toward Ash, a thought taking shape.
entries.text: At the Hearth, the morning light spills across the common room as Wren turns toward Ash, a thought taking shape. "Ash, the market's first light—a stallholder's cart is stuck in the mud. Want to come help? It's a small coin, but it's a start." Ash meets Wren's gaze, a slow nod following as the offer settles. "Aye, that's the plan. Let's go — I've got a hand to spare and a knack for wheels." With that, the two of them rise from the Hearth, setting out toward the market's first light.

entries.title: The hearth fire crackles low as the afternoon settles over Hearth.
entries.text: The hearth fire crackles low as the afternoon settles over Hearth. "Come on, Ash, let's not keep Marg waiting—she'll think we've forgotten her cart." Without another word, Ash turns and heads toward Market. Wren follows at Ash's side, quickening the pace toward Market. Back at Hearth, Old Marg waits by the door, arms folded, watching the road.

entries.title: The Market hums around them as Ash catches sight of Old Marg's cart, still sunk in the mud near her stall.
entries.text: The Market hums around them as Ash catches sight of Old Marg's cart, still sunk in the mud near her stall. "Marg, we're here for that wheel. Show me where it's stuck and I'll get my shoulder to it." Ash gestures toward the cart, trying to draw Wren's attention to the work at hand. Wren looks the scene over, taking in the cart's position and the mud around the wheels. Old Marg stays put by the cart, patient and waiting for the pair to settle on a plan. "There she is, Old Marg—cart's still rooted by the looks of it. Let's get that wheel out proper." "Wren, what are you looking at? Marg's cart won't fix itself — let's get to it." "Right—let's see if it's the axle or just sunk deep. I'll take the spoke side if you take the wheel."

entries.title: At the Market, the cart's wheel has sunk past its hub in the mud.
entries.text: At the Market, the cart's wheel has sunk past its hub in the mud. "Marg, we're here for that wheel. Show me where it's stuck and I'll get my shoulder to it." Old Marg points to the darkest mud, telling Ash that's the spot, and instructs Wren to take the other side. "Marg, we've got your wheel—let's heave her out of that mud together." Wren communicates to Ash: he'll take the spoke side for the heave. "Spoke side it is. On three—heave." Ash observes the wheel's position, and Old Marg waits, preparing to brace the cart as they pull. "Aye, that's the way—both hands and a good heave. I'll brace the cart so it don't tip when she comes free."

entries.text: At the Market, the wagon's wheel is sunk deep in the mud, and the three of them gather around it. Ash calls to Wren, 'Wren, I've got the near side. Set your feet and pull when I say—heave!' Wren digs in her heels and answers, 'Ready—one, two, three, heave!' as she braces on the spoke side. Before the pull, Wren checks in with Old Marg, 'Marg, you ready? I've got the spoke side — on three we heave.' Old Marg nods, promising, 'Aye, Wren, that's the spirit—give her all you've got, and I'll shove from the back. Once she's free, I'll fetch us a mug of hot cider from my stores.' Old Marg also calls to Ash, 'Aye, heave! I've got my back against the cart's side—when she frees, don't let her rock back on you.' Ash urges Wren on, 'Wren, old Marg's just standing there waiting on us—let's not leave her hanging. You take the spoke side, I'll get my shoulder under the hub, and we'll have that wheel out of the mud before the bell rings.' Wren focuses on Ash's cue to 'Heave the wheel free now,' and Ash mirrors with 'Heave the wheel out together on three,' as they coordinate their efforts while Old Marg waits, ready to shove from behind.

entries.title: At the Market, the heavy cart stands stuck, its wheel sunk fast in the muddy lane.
entries.text: At the Market, the heavy cart stands stuck, its wheel sunk fast in the muddy lane. Ash calls out across the cart, ready to put their strength into the work. "Ready when you are, Marg. On three—heave now!" "I'm set—spoke side's mine. On your call, Ash—heave!" Wren speaks to Ash, counting off the pull and urging them to use everything they have, saying the wheel is nearly free. Ash reports that Wren has headed off to Hearth, and tells Old Marg they'll see the job through together, bracing the cart and getting under the hub to free it before the light fades. "Easy, Ash—when she pops loose she'll lurch, so brace your knees. I'll shove the cart bed from here." Old Marg urges one final coordinated heave on three now that both are braced.

entries.title: The cart has finally ground to a stop here at the Market, its wheel sunk fast in the mud and stone.
entries.text: The cart has finally ground to a stop here at the Market, its wheel sunk fast in the mud and stone. Old Marg signals to Ash—one more heave on three, now that it's just the two of them. She'll push the cart bed while Ash pulls the hub, and they'll have her out before full dark. Ash gets ready, bracing the cart wheel and heaving once more alongside the old woman. "One more good shove and she's out—I'm putting my whole weight on the cart side. Watch your footing, Ash, here we go!" "Right, Marg—brace the bed and I'll set my shoulder under the hub. On three: heave!"

entries.title: At Hearth, a hush settles over the scene.
entries.text: At Hearth, a hush settles over the scene.

entries.title: At the Hearth, a quiet stillness settles over the scene.
entries.text: At the Hearth, a quiet stillness settles over the scene. Wren remains in place, holding steady as the moments pass.

entries.title: The Market, crowded and loud, presses in around the cart. The wheel is stuck fast, and the two of them stand braced agai
entries.text: The Market, crowded and loud, presses in around the cart. The wheel is stuck fast, and the two of them stand braced against it. Old Marg calls out one last plan to Ash: a single heave on three to free the wheel. Ash waits, gripping the spoke, ready for the count. "On three, Marg—heave!" "Ash, you've gone quiet. Don't lose heart now—grip the spoke, I'll heave with you. One last push, and we'll laugh about this over a hot drink."

entries.title: The two of them stand at the edge of the Market, the cart wedged firm. Ash plants both feet and calls out for one more h
entries.text: The two of them stand at the edge of the Market, the cart wedged firm. Ash plants both feet and calls out for one more heave, bracing for the strain. Old Marg answers from the other side, steady and calm. "Easy, Ash — I've got the other side braced. Give me the count and we'll pop her free." With a groan of wood and a shared effort, the cart pops free from the rut, rolling free at last. Ash straightens, wiping a sleeve across the brow, and looks over at Old Marg with a tired smile. "Good, let's roll her to the stall — and I'll take that tale with the hot drink you promised. It's been a long haul, but we got her free." The pair begin rolling the cart through the bustling Market, heading for the stall where the tale of the copper coin awaits.

entries.title: At Hearth, the quiet settles around Wren as she stands still, simply waiting.
entries.text: At Hearth, the quiet settles around Wren as she stands still, simply waiting.

entries.title: At the Hearth, dawn edges closer and the market still sleeps.
entries.text: At the Hearth, dawn edges closer and the market still sleeps. Old Marg looks to Ash and says, "Ash, we're here at last. Help me push the cart to the stall—then I'll pay you that copper and tell you the tale." Ash crouches by the wheel, and speaks to Old Marg: "Marg, if the axle's cracked we can't just heave—let's look underneath first. If it's only the hub, we can still shift her, but if the wood's split we'll need to brace it or carry the goods the rest of the way." Old Marg answers Ash: "We're here at last, Ash—the mud's behind us. Come, let's set the cart under the stall awning, then I'll tell you how this cart survived the Great Flood of Thorn Hollow, and the copper coin's yours as promised." Ash attempts to communicate with Old Marg about a final coordinated heave before sunrise. Old Marg attempts to communicate with Ash about checking the axle and a stall plan. Ash sees Wren arriving and calls out: "Wren, good to see you. Marg and I are still at it—the wheel's nearly free. Come lend a shoulder, and we'll have her out before the market stirs." Wren goes to Market.

entries.text: At the Market, the cart stands still as Ash, Old Marg, and Wren pause around it. Ash tries to catch Old Marg's eye, gesturing toward the axle — the one that took the jest of the splinter — wanting to check it before anyone heaves again. Wren, too, moves to speak with Ash — the same thought: check the axle and see if it can be fixed before the market opens its gates. Old Marg gestures toward the wheel. "Wheel's free, Ash—let's get the cart to the stall and I'll tell you the copper coin tale." "Good work, Marg—let's get rolling then. I'd like to hear that copper coin tale before the market opens." "Ash, a sound head on your shoulders—checking the axle before we throw ourselves at it again. Let's kneel and look at the join, see if it's split or just tired. If it's sound, we heave once more and be done." "Good call, Ash. Let's put that split to the test — I'll take the far side and trace the crack while you brace the hub." "Ash, let's look at that axle proper — if it's the pin, we can drive a new one in before the crowd. Feel along the crack and tell me how deep it goes." "Marg, I can take the other side of the cart bed—together we'll roll it to the stall before the light gets busy. And I'd love to hear that tale once we're parked."
